extracted.intended_audience: student journalists / reporters learning how to write news reports about fires and accidents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars for writing news stories about fires, explosions, collisions and other accidents: what facts to gather, which actors to quote, and how to structure casualty and investigation details. Emphasizes names, locations, causes, rescue actions, investigations, and human-interest elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: State probable cause and contributing factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the believed origin and contributing conditions (for example: 'A glowing match, carelessly tossed into a baby carriage... is believed to have started the fire' and 'Poor lighting in the hallways may have been an indirect cause of the fire').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute the cause with appropriate hedging when uncertain ("is believed to have started"), list indirect causes (poor lighting, careless smoking), and report inspection findings that support cause hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report official orders, inspections, and enforcement status
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether required safety orders had been issued and their enforcement progress (e.g., 'The orders were for the enclosure of an unenclosed stairway... and for the installation of an interior fire alarm system. Both orders had been turned over to the legal department for enforcement, and work on the stairway enclosure was in progress the day before the fire. Plans for the fire alarm system were approved Oct. 22').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include dates, which department issued orders, whether work was underway, and if communications with authorities had been severed or restored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify victims with names, ages, occupations
rubrics_metrics.description: List identified victims by name, age, and occupation or status (examples: 'Bernard Lynde, thirty-five, a laborer; Edward J. Ryan, thirty-five, a linchman; Louis Detter, fifty-three, a laborer').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also note unidentified victims, counts by location/floor, and family/boarder relationships where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide precise location and time details
rubrics_metrics.description: Give specific addresses, building numbers, neighborhood descriptors and time references (e.g., 'lodging house fire at No. 1516 Eighth avenue early yesterday morning').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention block, cross-streets, facility names and exact times where known to orient readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe rescue and response efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail actions taken by watchmen, police, firemen and bystanders in rescue efforts (e.g., 'Sergt. John Butler ... ran to the roof ... and assisted fifteen of the men to safety' and the account of Mounted Patrolman Dowling catching a runaway horse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include names, ranks, tools used (ladders, extension ladders, fire ladders), sequence of actions, injuries sustained by rescuers, and any extraordinary heroism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include investigations and responsible authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Report which authorities are investigating and the scope of inquiries (District-Attorney, Coroner, Fire Marshal, Public Service Commission, State Industrial Commission, company investigations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name investigating officials, outline multiple concurrent inquiries, and note any sought witnesses or missing persons (e.g., licensed blaster who disappeared).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report technical and structural details affecting outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Note building and vehicle features that affected casualties (fire escapes, unenclosed stairways, windows, type of street cars—wooden vs steel, broken gas/water mains, dynamite handling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how these features influenced the event (e.g., 'old wooden cars' crumpled; gas mains laid along curb limited damage) and quote officials arguing for structural changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide casualty counts and injury breakdowns
rubrics_metrics.description: Give totals of dead and injured and break down numbers by location or group when possible (examples: 'Seven persons were killed and eighty-five injured' and lists of those killed/seriously injured).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify where injured were taken (which hospitals), severity (fatally burned, probably fatally burned), and list names of the dead when known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use eyewitness and official quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include direct quotations from officials, rescuers, witnesses and experts (e.g., 'The Pain people thought they were absolutely protected against accidents,' said O'Donnell).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quotes to convey responsibility, opinion, procedural context, or human reaction; attribute clearly and preserve hedging or certainty in the source's words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply human-interest and background details
rubrics_metrics.description: Add personal and background information about victims and actors to humanize the story (family relations, occupations, short biographies, anecdotes—e.g., the baby in the runaway-wagon story or the librarian's career and family).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use such details to contextualize loss and make readers empathize, but keep factual and sourced information separate from speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronicle sequence of events and immediate aftermath
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrate the step-by-step progression before, during and after the incident (what happened first, crowd reaction, rescue chronology, subsequent service suspensions and restorations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear timeline so readers understand causation and the flow of rescue and investigation activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention legal and financial consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Report potential or actual legal actions, liabilities and financial context (damage suits, liability under workmen's compensation, insurance coverage, contract amounts and bonds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name companies and officers, state bond amounts and withheld payments, and note the company's assets if relevant to potential claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe sensory and vivid physical details
rubrics_metrics.description: Use concrete, vivid descriptions of damage and injuries to convey severity (examples: 'the car crumpled like pasteboard', 'two wheels passed over his chest', 'tossed into a blazing pool of gasoline').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for precise, evocative language grounded in observable facts; avoid melodrama and ensure descriptions are verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report prior warnings, inspections and compliance rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Note prior inspections, warnings given to property owners, and compliance statistics when available (for example: 'After an inspection of the district about ten days ago all the property owners were warned... The inspection disclosed that about 70 per cent of the houses were poorly lighted').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this material to show systemic context and whether the incident followed from known hazards or enforcement failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note transportation and service impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Report interruptions to public transit and services and projected duration (e.g., 'The Seventh Avenue car service was suspended south of Thirty-second Street, and it will be at least a week...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include alternative arrangements, extent of suspension, and expected timeline for resumption.
